facts.text: Mustang earned its name from nearby Mustang Creek, which was called either for the grapes that grew there or for the wild ponies roaming the area in the 1850s.
The town incorporated in 1973 so that it could legally sell alcohol in what had been a dry Navarro County.
On October 30, 1973, Mustang voters approved beer sales, making the town one of the first in the county to offer alcoholic beverages.
In December 2021, entrepreneur Mark Cuban purchased Mustang’s 77‑acre town for roughly $2 million, turning it into a virtual ghost town with vacant structures.
Back in 1940, Mustang had just fifty residents and two businesses; by 1951 it boasted a store, filling station, and an icehouse.
Groundwater from the Trinity Aquifer supports local needs, yet overpumping threatens depletion, while oil, gas, limestone, and sand shape the area’s land use.
